implementation_summary: Added an ingest-time per-type actor-rule gate to chatHandler.ts (a new module-private gateAnnouncement() function, run on every kind-9 rumor's parseStructured(content) result, strictly before deps.appendMessage/setChatVersion/incrementUnread/markAsRead). group_renamed and invite_cancelled require an admin actor (via a new isGroupAdmin dep). invite_lifecycle requires an admin actor for every event, and additionally roster-gates the subject at ingest ONLY for event='accepted' (via a new isGroupMember dep) — 'invited'/'declined' render unconditionally as unverified claims (AC-ANNOUNCE-2). member_admitted (defensive, no live producer) gets the same admin+roster gate as accepted (AC-ANNOUNCE-1/3). leave_intent gates subject===sender (S3 Stage-2 review fold-in — the kind-9 DEPARTURE ANNOUNCEMENT mirrors leaveHandler.ts's kind-13 rule). poll_close is creator-gated against the stored Poll (new getPoll/loadVotes deps reused from the existing poll-store accessors) and its persisted content is REWRITTEN to a tally recomputed from stored PollVote rows via a newly-extracted, shared computeTally (app/src/lib/marmot/pollTally.ts, also now used by pollHandler.ts) — never the closer's self-reported results/totalVoters (F1, S5 Stage-2 review fold-in). call_notice is never actor-gated (AC-ANNOUNCE-4) and its ChatBox.tsx render branch was fixed to source the displayed actor from msg.senderPubkey instead of the payload's self-reported initiator field. Every admin/roster/poll lookup in the gate is wrapped in .catch() to fail closed on a throwing/indeterminate provider (VQ-S6-006). isGroupAdmin is wired at the composition root (MarmotContext.tsx) to a new isRegisteredGroupAdmin export on messageEdits/api.ts, which wraps the ALREADY-registered GroupAdminsProvider singleton rather than instantiating a second lookup (VQ-S6-002); isGroupMember wraps the pre-existing getLiveMemberPubkeys live-roster accessor. A new integrated-e2e spec (groups-announcement-roster-gate.spec.ts) drives a real invite+accept+leave flow through the app UI (never raw WebSocket) proving AC-ANNOUNCE-3: the accepted announcement remains visible after the admitted member later leaves — the ingest-time decision is never retroactively re-evaluated.

scope_deviation.rationale: Not pre-authorized by a synchronous coordinator round-trip within this spawn — self-flagged for the lead's record (VQ-S6-012 in verification.json; full rationale also in architecture.json's private_files SCOPE NOTE). Two categories: (1) the four new ChatHandlerDeps fields (isGroupAdmin/isGroupMember/getPoll/loadVotes) require composition-root wiring — registerHandlers.ts and MarmotContext.tsx are the only place live closures exist; this exact pair of files was ALSO expanded-into by S5 for an analogous reason (see S5's own architecture.json 'coordinator-authorized scope expansion' note), suggesting a recurring staleness in how scope.includes is derived for stories whose ACs require new composition-root dep-wiring. (2) AC-ANNOUNCE-4's literal wording ('is not rendered as the actor') cannot be satisfied by chatHandler.ts alone since it does not control rendering; architecture.md's own Scope section explicitly names the call_notice render fix ('stop rendering initiator from the payload') as part of this story's substance.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The story's declared scope.includes (stories.json) named only 3 files, but this story's actual substance — architecture.md's own 'hidden coupling... biggest work item' framing — always required composition-root wiring (registerHandlers.ts, MarmotContext.tsx) and, less obviously until deep in discovery, a UI render fix (ChatBox.tsx's call_notice branch) to make AC-ANNOUNCE-4 true in the observable product, not just in an internal field. Diagnosing WHERE the poll_close F1 fold-in and the leave_intent departure-announcement fold-in needed to attach also took significant investigation: neither is a new handler type, both are pre-existing announcement renderers whose actual producers/wire-shapes had to be traced through several indirection layers (PollStoreContext.tsx's closePoll, profileHandler.ts's accept-producer, cancelInvitationImpl.ts) before the gate's per-type switch could be written with confidence that it wouldn't reject any legitimate existing producer.
retrospective.surprised_by: group_renamed and member_admitted currently have ZERO live production producers (verified by exhaustive grep) — both are purely defensive/legacy per architecture.md's own note about member_admitted, but the same turned out to be true of group_renamed too, which architecture.md's per-type table doesn't call out. This meant admin-gating both types carried no regression risk against any real sender, which simplified the implementation but was not something I could have assumed from the spec text alone.
